headline.technical: WSJ reported stock futures rose and oil fell as investors returned to risk after last week's tech selloff; Brent is -7.68% (1d) at 108.60, the VIX is 18.86, and the S&P 500 closed -1.82% on Friday.
headline.layman: Oil got cheaper and US stock futures pointed higher after a rough week for tech shares, but investors stay cautious before Tuesday's US midterm elections.

global.title: Cautious return to risk as oil falls; AI doubts and midterms in focus

status.technical: WSJ reported stock futures rose and Treasury yields eased as falling oil encouraged a cautious return to risk after last week's tech selloff. Brent is -7.68% (1d) at 108.60 and the VIX is 18.86. WSJ also reported the dollar fell to a one-month low.
status.layman: WSJ said stock futures rose and oil fell as investors cautiously came back to risk after last week's tech selloff. WSJ also said the US dollar slipped to a one-month low.

consequence.technical: If U.S.-Iran diplomacy keeps pushing oil lower, yield and inflation pressure could ease; Reuters noted, however, that the risk of a rise in a key US interest rate remains even after the recent fall.
consequence.layman: If the US and Iran keep talking and oil keeps getting cheaper, price pressures could ease. But Reuters says the risk of higher US interest rates has not gone away.

impact.technical: Fuel-intensive sectors are exposed: Ryanair's CEO told CNBC European fares could rise by up to 20% in 2027 as its fuel bill jumps by $2.2 billion, and the Straits Times reported China's top three airlines are heading for full-year losses on fuel costs.
impact.layman: Airlines feel high fuel costs most. Ryanair's boss told CNBC fares could rise by up to 20% in 2027, and the Straits Times says China's big three airlines are heading for yearly losses.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after S&P 500 one-day falls larger than 1 standard deviation, the next day rose 48% of 154 times and the next 5 days rose 58% of 154 times (median 0.37%). Bloomberg quoted Morgan Stanley's Wilson saying any post-midterm selloff is likely to be short-lived.
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions: after days like Friday, the S&P 500 was higher 5 days later 58% of the time. Bloomberg quoted Morgan Stanley's Wilson saying any selloff after the vote is likely to be short-lived.

regions.title: Americas: tech-led fall on Friday, futures higher now

status.technical: Last close: S&P 500 -1.82%, Dow -1.09%, Nasdaq -2.86% (1d). The FT reported the global AI sell-off is easing after Nasdaq's worst month in over a year; Reuters reported Wall Street futures rose as AI stocks caught their breath.
status.layman: US stocks fell on Friday, with the Nasdaq down 2.86%. The Financial Times says the AI-driven selling is easing, and Reuters says US futures are higher.

consequence.technical: If investor concern over hyperscaler spending and AI returns persists, tech could stay under pressure; if the pause reported by Reuters holds, the futures strength could carry into the cash session.
consequence.layman: If worries about big AI spending stay, tech shares could keep wobbling. If the calm Reuters describes holds, the market could open firmer.

impact.technical: CNBC reported Democratic gains in Congress could bring tougher oversight of major companies and shift federal spending and regulatory policy, with defense, healthcare, crypto and AI named as areas to watch.
impact.layman: CNBC says if Democrats gain seats, big companies could face tougher oversight and government spending could shift. It names defense, healthcare, crypto and AI as areas to watch.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after Nasdaq one-day falls larger than 1 standard deviation, the next day rose 49% of 170 times and the next 5 days rose 54% of 169 times (median 0.34%).
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions: after big Nasdaq drops like Friday's, it was higher 5 days later 54% of the time.

regions.title: Europe: mostly firmer closes; France outlook cut, Alstom slides

status.technical: Closes: DAX 0.24%, CAC 40 0.41%, Euro Stoxx 50 0.41%, FTSE 100 0.07% (1d). Morningstar reported European stocks rose as oil fell on diplomacy hopes, while Yahoo Finance reported early slips as Fitch lowered France's credit outlook.
status.layman: European markets ended slightly higher. Morningstar linked gains to cheaper oil, while earlier in the day Yahoo Finance said stocks slipped after Fitch cut France's credit outlook.

consequence.technical: Economic Times reported French bond yields held steady despite the Fitch warning as investors weighed fiscal concerns against easing energy prices; if energy prices rebound, that balance could shift.
consequence.layman: France's borrowing costs stayed steady even after the Fitch warning, because easier energy prices offset worries. If energy prices jump again, that balance could change.

impact.technical: Alstom shares tumbled 28% after a profit warning; the Straits Times reported it now expects an adjusted Ebit margin of about 1% versus 6.5% previously. Bloomberg reported Belgium's prime minister offered his resignation after a budget dispute.
impact.layman: Train maker Alstom's shares fell 28% after it cut its profit forecast. Separately, Belgium's prime minister offered to resign after his coalition failed to agree a budget.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days the DAX rose over the next 5 days 57% of 855 times (median 0.37%) and the Euro Stoxx 50 rose 57% of 849 times (median 0.36%).
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions: after calm days like today, Germany's DAX was higher 5 days later 57% of the time.

regions.title: Asia-Pacific: China bounce on support, Korea and India up, ASX lower

status.technical: Closes (1d): Shanghai 1.08%, Shenzhen 1.63%, KOSPI 2.24%, Nifty 50 1.68%, Australia's ASX -0.58%. SCMP reported China's central bank would launch a swap facility channeling about US$15 billion into stocks after a record 12-week sell-off; Economic Times reported South Korea's October exports nearly doubled.
status.layman: China, Korea and India rose; Australia fell. Beijing is putting about US$15 billion into its stock market after a record 12-week slide, and South Korea reported its October exports nearly doubled.

consequence.technical: SCMP noted China's stocks got little relief from the latest support efforts; if regulators' measures fail to rebuild confidence, rallies may fade. Yahoo Finance Australia tied the ASX slump to interest rate anxiety ahead of the RBA decision.
consequence.layman: SCMP says the Chinese support has given little relief so far, so gains may not last. In Australia, worry about interest rates and an upcoming central bank decision weighed on shares.

impact.technical: Straits Times reported Asian factory growth is slowing as the US-Iran war threatens to offset AI gains; Taiwan's central bank eased exporter dollar-sale curbs after record foreign stock outflows.
impact.layman: Factories in key Asian economies are growing more slowly, the Straits Times says, as the US-Iran war offsets AI gains. Taiwan also loosened rules to support its currency after heavy foreign selling.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after Nifty 50 one-day rises larger than 1 standard deviation, the next day rose 57% of 175 times and the next 5 days rose 59% of 174 times (median 0.24%).
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions: after big one-day gains like India's today, the Nifty was higher 5 days later 59% of the time.

drivers.title: Oil: U.S.-Iran diplomacy hopes versus a prolonged war

status.technical: Brent is -7.68% (1d) at 108.60 and WTI -4.38% (1d) at 99.56. CNBC reported U.S. crude fell below $100 as both the U.S. and Iran pursue diplomacy; WSJ reported oil slid on signs Mideast escalation may be avoided for now.
status.layman: Oil dropped sharply today. CNBC says US crude fell below $100 because the US and Iran are both pursuing talks.

consequence.technical: Bloomberg reported the Iran war is dragging into its ninth month and Chilean investors are buying inflation-linked notes as oil rose to levels not seen since April; if diplomacy stalls, the FT said Gulf states brace for escalation.
consequence.layman: Bloomberg says the war has dragged on and investors are protecting themselves against rising prices. If the talks stall, the FT says Gulf countries fear things could get worse.

impact.technical: Real Macro's Jeff Currie said physical oil is pricing in a permanent regime shift, with long-dated Brent close to $99 a barrel. JM Financial flagged a $105 crude threshold for FII flows into India.
impact.layman: Oil expert Jeff Currie says the oil market is changing for good, with long-dated Brent near $99. A brokerage says crude above $105 matters for foreign money flowing into India.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after Brent one-day falls larger than 1 standard deviation, the next 5 days rose 54% of 168 times; look-alike days saw the next 21 days rise 1 of 5 times (median -3.64%).
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions: after sharp oil drops like today's, oil was higher 5 days later 54% of the time.

drivers.title: AI spending scrutiny and the tech selloff

status.technical: Economic Times reported the Nasdaq had its biggest single-day fall since June on concerns over hyperscaler spending and AI returns; Nasdaq closed -2.86% (1d). In the biggest names, Nvidia fell -4.22% and Broadcom -5.48% (1d).
status.layman: Tech shares dropped hard on Friday because investors doubt that huge AI spending will pay off, Economic Times says. Chip giants Nvidia and Broadcom fell the most among the biggest names.

consequence.technical: The Straits Times reported scrutiny is rising but Big Tech is unlikely to give up; if returns disappoint, Asia's chip-heavy economies could be affected, since the AI boom's fate may redefine Asia's outlook.
consequence.layman: The Straits Times says Big Tech is unlikely to back off AI. If the payoff disappoints, Asia, which makes most of the chips, could feel it.

impact.technical: Yahoo Finance reported Wall Street is bearish on hyperscalers Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Oracle; Alphabet is -12.61% over 5 days.
impact.layman: Yahoo Finance says Wall Street analysts are surprisingly negative on the big cloud-computing firms. Alphabet shares are down 12.61% over five days.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after Nasdaq one-day falls larger than 1 standard deviation, the next day rose 49% of 170 times; look-alike days saw the next 21 days rise 3 of 5 times (median 4.60%).
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions: after drops like Friday's, the Nasdaq was higher a month later in 3 of 5 similar past cases.

status.technical: Economic Times reported analysts anticipate potential Republican losses in the November 3 midterms. Bloomberg reported polls suggest Democrats are expected to make gains in the House and Senate. The VIX is 18.86.
status.layman: US midterm elections are on November 3. Polls suggest Democrats are expected to gain seats, according to Bloomberg.

consequence.technical: Economic Times said a divided government may heighten market volatility, although historical annualised returns remain largely unaffected. Bloomberg quoted Morgan Stanley's Wilson that any post-vote selloff is likely to be short-lived.
consequence.layman: A split government could make markets bumpier, but Economic Times says long-run returns have mostly not been affected. Morgan Stanley's Wilson expects any selling after the vote to be short.

impact.technical: CNBC reported Democratic gains could shift billions of dollars in federal spending and regulatory policy, touching defense, healthcare, crypto and AI. Rupee traders stayed cautious ahead of the vote.
impact.layman: CNBC says a change in Congress could redirect government money and rules in defense, healthcare, crypto and AI. Currency traders in India are also waiting.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: for the VIX, look-alike days saw the next 5 days rise 0 of 5 times (median -9.39%); after ordinary days it rose over 5 days 49% of 894 times.
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions: in similar past cases, the VIX fear gauge fell over the next 5 days in all 5 cases.

status.technical: WSJ reported US Treasury and European bond yields fell as oil dropped. The US 10-year yield closed at 4.93 (1d -1.20%); the dollar index is 101.68 (1d -0.19%). Economic Times reported Japan's 10-year yield held at 2.77%.
status.layman: Government borrowing costs fell as oil got cheaper, WSJ says. The US dollar eased too. Japan's 10-year yield held at 2.77%.

consequence.technical: Reuters said the risk of a rise in a key US interest rate remains even after the recent fall. Economic Times reported Goldman Sachs revised its Bank of England outlook, citing climbing energy costs and robust growth.
consequence.layman: Reuters warns US rates could still rise even after the recent dip. Goldman Sachs now sees the Bank of England possibly raising rates, because of energy costs and solid growth.

impact.technical: WSJ reported investors are focused this week on the Treasury's quarterly refunding details and monthly employment data. The ECB main refinancing rate is 2.65 % (macro:ecb_refi).
impact.layman: This week investors watch how the US government plans to borrow and the monthly jobs report. In Europe, the ECB's main rate is 2.65 %.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after US 10-year yield one-day falls larger than 1 standard deviation, the next 5 days rose 57% of 153 times (median 0.44%).
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions: after big yield drops like Friday's, yields were higher 5 days later 57% of the time.

drivers.title: India: foreign investor tax relief proposal and FII flows

status.technical: Business Standard reported Sebi proposed scrapping LTCG tax on foreign investors' equity gains. Nifty 50 closed 1.68% and Sensex 1.66% higher (1d); USD/INR is 94.90.
status.layman: India's market regulator Sebi has proposed removing a tax on long-term gains for foreign investors, Business Standard says. India's main indexes rose today.

consequence.technical: Bernstein's Venugopal Garre said a reduction in LTCG tax would be desirable but would not, by itself, trigger sustained FII inflows; JM Financial flagged crude at $105 as a threshold for FII flows.
consequence.layman: Bernstein's Venugopal Garre says the tax cut would help but would not alone bring lasting foreign money. JM Financial says oil prices matter too.

impact.technical: Economic Times reported FIIs raised stakes in 19 Nifty 50 companies in the September 2026 quarter. Business Standard reported a record Rs 84,400 crore of mainboard IPO fundraising in H1 FY27.
impact.layman: Foreign investors raised their stakes in 19 Nifty 50 companies last quarter. India's IPO market also raised a record Rs 84,400 crore in the first half of the fiscal year.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after Sensex one-day rises larger than 1 standard deviation, the next day rose 57% of 164 times and the next 5 days rose 56% of 163 times (median 0.39%).
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions: after big gains like today's, the Sensex was higher 5 days later 56% of the time.

events.layman: Americans vote on Tuesday. A split Congress could make markets bumpier, but past long-run returns were mostly unaffected.

events.title: US Treasury quarterly refunding and monthly employment data
events.technical: WSJ listed the Treasury's quarterly refunding announcement details and monthly employment data among this week's focus points for investors.
events.layman: This week the US government shares how it plans to borrow, and the monthly jobs numbers come out.

events.title: Apple earnings
events.technical: Yahoo Finance said US futures rose ahead of Apple earnings, alongside oil and election focus.
events.layman: Apple reports results soon, and investors are watching it along with oil and the elections.

events.title: Japan 10-year government bond auction
events.technical: Economic Times said JGB yields were mixed ahead of a series of auctions including a 10-year sale on Thursday; the 10-year yield held at 2.77%.
events.layman: Japan sells 10-year government bonds on Thursday. Investors are watching what rates it has to pay.

events.title: RBA and Bank of England rate decisions
events.technical: Mint reported the RBA decision looms; Yahoo Finance said traders brace for the BoE and Goldman Sachs sees a possible rate rise.
events.layman: Central banks in Australia and the UK are due to decide on interest rates, and investors are on edge.
